research_goal: Create level-based kickboxing teaching, readiness, assessment, promotion, hold, and regression logic for SFTC.

source_refs.title: WAKO Rules
source_refs.notes: Used for rule-set and discipline differences affecting progression.

source_refs.title: GLORY Rules
source_refs.notes: Used for K-1 style competition context.

technical_principles.summary: A user can be intermediate in fitness bag work but beginner in low-kick defense, sparring, K-1 knees, or point-fighting tactics. The backend should unlock content by domain readiness.
Beginners progress from stance and single-strike mechanics to combinations, defense, controlled contact, and only then open sparring.
Advanced kickboxing is not just harder conditioning; it is rule-set-specific tactics, opponent reads, fight-week planning, and contact-load management.

beginner.definition: Learning stance, guard, footwork, basic punches, basic kicks, defense, control, and safe training habits.
unlock: no-contact or light technical partner drills

intermediate.definition: Connecting combinations, defensive responses, style choices, rule-set tactics, conditioning rounds, and controlled sparring.

advanced.definition: Rule-set-specific fight planning, opponent preparation, high-quality sparring management, speed/power conversion, competition taper, and tactical adaptation.

sport_training_rules.rule: Assess kickboxing readiness by domain: stance, footwork, punch mechanics, kick mechanics, defense, low-kick defense, combinations, sparring contact, K-1 knees, and rule-set IQ.
recommended_action: Use beginner drills in weak domains even if the athlete is advanced in fitness or another combat sport.
Unlock sparring, low-kick contact, knees, and advanced tactics separately.
blocked_action: global advanced label unlocking all contact work
hard sparring from fitness kickboxing history alone

planning_rules.rule: Select kickboxing drills by rule set, contact level, and domain readiness, not only by global experience.
recommended_action: Keep no-sparring fitness users on technical bag/pad progressions.
Use low-kick and K-1 domains only when rule set supports them.
Use point-fighting speed/timing domains for point fighters.
blocked_action: hard contact from global intermediate label
low-kick work for full-contact-only users unless cross-training
Muay Thai clinch as default kickboxing

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build a safe foundation for kickboxing before contact complexity.
progression_steps: Rear and lead round kick mechanics with stance recovery.
Partner feed with controlled defense and exit.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build rule-set-specific offense, defense, and round management.
progression_steps: Identify rule set and scoring priorities.
Apply in constrained sparring or technical rounds.
Review pain, fatigue, and skill quality.

sport_skill_assessments.summary: Assess whether a beginner is ready for limited technical contact.
metrics: stance remains stable under partner feed
no head, wrist, shoulder, hip, knee, ankle, shin pain escalation
hold_if: pain or symptoms increase after sessions

minimum_evidence: stance, guard, jab-cross, round kick, and basic defense are stable
no worsening pain or symptom trend
promote_when: athlete combines attack-defense-exit under moderate fatigue
can perform controlled partner drills safely
rule-set preference is known or safe default is maintained
sport_level_transition_rules.backend_action: Recommend intermediate domain unlocks: combination chains, defensive counters, rule-set-specific tactics, and constrained sparring if contact level permits.

minimum_evidence: contact load tolerated without symptom escalation
promote_when: athlete adapts tactics to style/rule set
sport_level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock advanced fight-camp planning, opponent-style tactics, high-quality speed/power blocks, and competition-week taper logic.
